dbpcm_warehouse.accrual_events.grain_note: Event-level accrual log. No reliable exposed row id; do NOT assume uniqueness by EmployeeCode, RequestDate, EarnCode, or Status. Granularity is ONE ROW PER DAY of a request (see RequestDate), so SUM(Hours) over a RequestDate range is exact. Logical analysis grain: one accrual event/day row.

"Who reports to X", span-of-control, and org rollups must match Primary…Quaternary SupervisorEmployeeName against employee names, which is non-unique and breaks on duplicate/changed names. dbpcm_warehouse.payroll.description: Payroll register line-item table. Contains paycheck components such as earnings, deductions, taxes, benefits, employer taxes, and net-pay distributions. Not one row per paycheck.
dbpcm_warehouse.payroll.grain_note: Payroll register LINE ITEMS — one row per pay component, not one row per paycheck. No exposed unique row id (TransactionNumber is NOT unique). Multiple rows share the same EmployeeCode + PayDate. Logical analysis grains for GROUP BY: a "paycheck" = EmployeeCode + PayDate (often + pay-period dates); an employee's period earnings = SUM(Amount) WHERE RegisterType='EARN' grouped to EmployeeCode + period. Blueprints must declare their own result grain; this base table is unverifiable.
